DRY-RUN COMPLETION VERIFICATION: FAIL — four REAL gaps, found before CI turned green. This is work
still owed on this story, not a criterion-wording problem. Recording precisely so the next session can
close them without re-deriving.

GAP 1 — the credential test asserts the WRONG ARTIFACT.
  Criterion: "no credential material from base_url or api_key appears anywhere in the PERSISTED SIDECAR
  PAYLOAD". My test (tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py::test_credentials_in_base_url_never_reach_the_record)
  asserts on the record returned by `provenance_for` — NOT on the persisted payload. Those are different
  artifacts: the record is one key inside a payload that also carries model, runner, coverage, findings
  and more, and `cfg.api_key` flows near that path independently. The oracle must serialize the PERSISTED
  payload (via the sidecar build_payload, as written for all three sidecars) and assert neither the
  username, the password, nor the api_key appears anywhere in it. The current test would pass even if a
  credential leaked through some OTHER payload field.

GAP 2 — the legacy/back-compat test was never written.
  Criterion: "a legacy payload lacking provider_provenance still loads and its signature verifies". This
  is the whole justification for the additive-only design, and there is no test for it. Pattern to follow:
  tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_sidecar.py::test_sidecar_phase_parser_accepts_legacy_and_execution_payloads
  is the one existing legacy-payload test in the tree. NOTE the signing seam: the sidecar payload is NOT
  what gets signed — signing binds (ticket_id, manifest) where the manifest is a list of "key: value"
  strings (plan_review/manifest.py:386, _commands/transition_close.py:451). So "the signature still
  verifies" is a claim about the MANIFEST, and the test must exercise that, not the payload dict.

GAP 3 — docs/event-schema.md was never updated.
  Criterion: "documents the field as additive and optional". Purely undone; no code involved.

GAP 4 — the [operator-attested] live evidence is missing.
  Criterion: a real `rebar review-plan` run writes a sidecar whose `provider_provenance.tier` matches the
  configured provider, shown in a ticket comment. Needs an actual gate run, then the observed
  provider_provenance object quoted here. Cheapest path: run review-plan on any ticket with --ref HEAD and
  read the emitted REVIEW_RESULT sidecar.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE AND SHOULD NOT BE REDONE: `provenance_for` exists in capabilities.py taking only
primitives (leaf-module invariant preserved), is wired through runner.run() reusing the caps record
resolved once, and is persisted by all THREE sidecars (plan_review :630, completion :207 and :225,
code_review :106). Eight unit tests pass, including a mutation-verified credential check on the RECORD
(.hostname vs .netloc) — that check is sound as far as it goes, it just does not satisfy criterion 1,
which is about the persisted payload.
